To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the specific activity of microsomal coumarin-6-hydroxylasewas significantly lower in patients with cirrhosis, chronic alcoholic hepatitis and chronic active hepatitis than in patients with acute and chronic persistent hepatitis and healthy subjects.

the activity of the microsomal enzyme system that hydroxylates coumarin to its 7-hydroxy derivative was found to be lower in the liver of patients with cirrhosis, chronic alcoholic hepatitis or chronic active hepatitis.

the specific activity of microsomal coumarin- 7-hydroxilase was measured in needle biopsies from normal subjects and from patients with liver disease, and that patients with cirrhosis, chronic fatty hepatitis or chronic active hepatitis showed significantly lower levels of hydroxylas activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method of measuring coumarin- 7-hydrox-ylase in microsomes obtained from liver biopsy specimens of patients with liver disease and normal controls.
the metabolism of drugs in the liver.
the metabolism of coumarin in human liver and its application to the study of human liver diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the specific activity of microsomal coumarin- 7-hydroxilase is lower in patients with cirrhosis than in normal individuals and that this is not due to genetic factors, but to a specific loss of enzyme activity.
the specific activity of the coumarin- 7-hydrox ylase is lower in liver microsomal preparations from patients with cirrhosis than in normal controls.
the mean specific activity of microsomal coumarin- 7-hydroxycase in patients with chronic liver diseases is lower than that in healthy individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coumarin-6a-hydroxylating system is present in liver microsomal fractions prepared by a simple procedure from needle biopsied human liver tissue and that this activity can be used as a measure of hepatic drug-metabolizing capacity.

coumarin-6a-hydroxylation and 7-hydroxlation in human liver microsomes are catalysed by different enzymes, and that the activity of the former is higher than that of the latter in the liver of healthy individuals.

the specific activity of the coumarin- 7-hydroxyselase in microsomes of needle biopsies from patients with cirrhosis, chronic fatty hepatitis and chronic active hepatitis is significantly lower than in the normal controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coumarin-6A and 7A are potent inhibitors of the CYP1A1 enzyme.
coumarin 7-hydroxilase activity can be measured in liver microsome from needle biopsy samples, and that this activity may be used to evaluate hepatic function in liver diseases.
we can now use this assay to measure the activity of coumarins in a patient’s blood.
